data.text: **Question:** What is the difference between abstract class and interface? (When to use which?)
Use interface for capabilities (can-do), use abstract class for base behavior (is-a). Modern C# allows default interface methods, blurring the line.

Interfaces define contracts. Abstract classes provide base implementation. Use interface for multiple capabilities. Use abstract class for shared base behavior. Default interface methods (C# 8+) allow some implementation.
